properties.name: The lens finally rides the skill response — and the drift it accumulated was a real bug
properties.rationale:
🛑 A MONTH ON A BRANCH COST TWO REAL DEFECTS, AND THAT IS THE DURABLE LESSON.

**1. THE WRITE-LOCK BUG, which would have shipped silently.** `lens_for_response` took `self.write_lock()` to perform a READ. Harmless when written on 2026-08-19; not harmless now. On 2026-08-26 `write_lock` became fallible AND began refusing outright on a `--read-only` server. Landing the branch unchanged would have returned `None` on every read-only deployment — **disabling the lens precisely on the surface a stranger reads the design through, which is where speaking their vocabulary matters most.** Computing a lens is a read; the original said otherwise and no test would have caught it, because no test ran against a read-only service. Now `self.graph.read()`.

**2. THE FIVE HANDLER TESTS NEVER RAN BECAUSE THEY NEVER COMPILED.** The commit message called them "unrun". They were unrunnable: `GetSkillReq` / `ListSkillsReq` had moved from `skills` to `tools::skills_tools` in the tool-surface refactor, and `name` on two request types had become `Option<String>`. **"Unrun tests" and "tests that do not compile" are different states and the commit recorded the softer one.** All five pass now, alongside the six core tests.

⭐ THE CHERRY-PICK CONFLICTED AND THE CONFLICT WAS INFORMATION. `skills.rs` was refactored after the branch: the tool handlers moved to `tools/skills_tools.rs` and the file kept only helpers. Resolving the conflict textually would have re-added structs that already exist elsewhere. The lens was instead applied BY HAND to the two files it actually belongs in — which is how the write-lock bug was noticed at all.

📌 WHY IT MATTERED ENOUGH TO GO BACK FOR. A user reported twice, months apart, that reflow2 "still speaks its own jargon and never asks who I am". Both reports were correct and neither was a missing idea: the only two skills that instruct asking are `where-am-i` and `capture-intent`, which a regular user runs and a new user does not. **A mechanism that only fires on the path its author walks is indistinguishable from a working one, from where the author stands** — and the design recorded the capability, so every reading of the graph said the mechanism existed.

⚠️ AND THE LIMIT THE CAPABILITY ALWAYS NAMED IS UNCHANGED: the tests prove the lens computes and is attached. They do not prove an agent ACTS on it, and nothing proves the translation is any good. This closes delivery. **Whether the words that come out are the reader's words remains unmeasured**, and the trial that would measure it — a real gap list narrated to a reader with a stated non-software background — is still the missing instrument.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary: `get_skill` and `list_skills` now carry a `lens` field: who the design knows how to speak to, or a plain statement that it knows nobody. Moves `cap:the-skill-response-carries-the-lens` from `in_progress` to `realized` — it was built 2026-08-19 on branch `lens-hint-rides-the-loop-rail` (commit e01c760), deliberately not marked realized at the v0.36.0 cut, and never merged. Verified live against the real binary: a `get_skill` response now returns keys [body, description, lens, name]. Workspace suite 1835 passed / 0 failed across 163 binaries, reconciling exactly against 1824 + 11 across 161 + 2.
